wiki-rail-nigeria.title: Rail transport in Nigeria (Wikipedia)
wiki-rail-nigeria.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-rail-nigeria.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-rail-nigeria.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-rail-nigeria.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Construction from Lagos to Ibadan began in March 1896; the Lagos Government Railway began operations in March 1901 and was extended to Minna in 1911, where it met the Baro-Kano railway built by Northern Nigeria between 1907 and 1911; the two were amalgamated in 1912; the railway reached Nguru in 1930. After coal was discovered at Udi, the Eastern Railway was built to Port Harcourt between 1913 and 1916, extended to Kaduna via Kafanchan in 1927, and to Maiduguri between 1958 and 1964.

wiki-baro.title: Baro, Nigeria (Wikipedia)
wiki-baro.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-baro.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-baro.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-baro.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. A small port town on the Niger, at the limit of river navigation; the starting point of the Baro to Kano railway, built by the Northern Nigerian Protectorate under Lugard from 1907 to 1911. Coordinates 8.583 N 6.417 E.

wiki-jebba.title: Jebba (Wikipedia)
wiki-jebba.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-jebba.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-jebba.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-jebba.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. A ferry carried people across the Niger from 1911 while the bridges were built; the article says the railway line reached Jebba in 1916. Coordinates 9.154 N 4.812 E. This differs from the railway overview, which has the line at Minna in 1911.

wiki-lagos-colony.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-lagos-colony.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-lagos-colony.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-lagos-colony.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. In August 1861 a British naval force entered Lagos and annexed it as a British colony by the Lagos Treaty of Cession.

wiki-apapa.title: Apapa Port Complex (Wikipedia)
wiki-apapa.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-apapa.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-apapa.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-apapa.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Dredging of Lagos harbour and two stone moles: in 1913 the works were completed and ocean-going ships could enter. In 1919 a 180-foot wharf was built at Apapa, chosen as the terminus of the western railway; by the late 1920s it was the busiest port for produce from the Western and Northern provinces.

wiki-federation-nigeria.title: Federation of Nigeria (Wikipedia)
wiki-federation-nigeria.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-federation-nigeria.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)

wiki-federation-nigeria.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. A predecessor of modern Nigeria from 1954 to 1963, with its capital at Lagos; independent on 1 October 1960 by the Nigeria Independence Act 1960.

wiki-enugu.title: Enugu (Wikipedia)
wiki-enugu.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-enugu.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-enugu.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-enugu.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. By 1909 coal was found under the village of Enugwu Ngwo in the Udi area; by 1913 it was confirmed in commercially viable quantities, and land was acquired for the Eastern Line railway and a colliery. Coordinates 6.453 N 7.511 E.

wiki-port-harcourt.title: Port Harcourt (Wikipedia)
wiki-port-harcourt.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-port-harcourt.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-port-harcourt.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-port-harcourt.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Founded in 1912 by Lugard to export the coal that the geologist Albert Ernest Kitson had discovered at Enugu in 1909; the colonial government made the people of Diobu cede their land, and building the port-town began in 1912; named Port Harcourt in August 1913 after Lewis Harcourt, Secretary of State for the Colonies. Coordinates 4.824 N 7.034 E.

wiki-zungeru.title: Zungeru (Wikipedia)
wiki-zungeru.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-zungeru.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-zungeru.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-zungeru.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Capital of the British protectorate of Northern Nigeria from 1902 until 1916; British forces occupied it in September 1902; Lugard chose it over Jebba and Lokoja for its central position. Coordinates 9.8 N 6.15 E.

wiki-colonial-nigeria.title: Colonial Nigeria (Wikipedia)
wiki-colonial-nigeria.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-colonial-nigeria.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-colonial-nigeria.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-colonial-nigeria.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Britain annexed Lagos in 1861 and established the Oil River Protectorate in 1884; other powers acknowledged British dominance at the 1885 Berlin Conference; from 1886 to 1899 much of the area was ruled by the Royal Niger Company under charter; in 1900 the Southern and Northern Nigeria Protectorates passed from the company to the Crown; Lagos Colony was merged into Southern Nigeria (1906) and in 1914 Southern and Northern Nigeria were combined as the Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria; independence on 1 October 1960.

wiki-calabar.title: Calabar (Wikipedia)
wiki-calabar.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-calabar.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-calabar.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-calabar.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. A seaport since the 16th century, exporting palm oil; a major port of the Atlantic slave trade; headquarters of the European administration in the Niger Delta until 1906, when the seat of government moved to Lagos. Coordinates 4.977 N 8.338 E.

countrystudies-unification.title: Nigeria: a country study, "Unification of Nigeria" (Library of Congress, 1991)
countrystudies-unification.author: Helen Chapin Metz (ed.), Federal Research Division, Library of Congress
countrystudies-unification.rights: US government work, public domain; facts cited only.
countrystudies-unification.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Lugard returned in 1912 to set in motion the merger of the northern and southern protectorates; harbour dredging and road and railway building opened Nigeria to economic development; port and transport improvements during the First World War furthered it.

wiki-kafanchan.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. A railway junction town; its station was built in 1927. Coordinates 9.583 N 8.293 E.

wiki-makurdi.title: Makurdi (Wikipedia)

wiki-makurdi.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. Divided by the River Benue; the railway bridge was built in 1932; on the main line north from Port Harcourt. Coordinates 7.733 N 8.5 E.

wiki-maiduguri.checked: Opened 1 Nov 2026. The railway was extended here in 1964, at the end of the line from Port Harcourt through Enugu, Kafanchan, Kuru and Bauchi. Coordinates 11.837 N 13.154 E.
